Revenue increased 62% to US$307.8 million

Gross profit expanded 128% to US$7.5 million

EBITDA rose 622% to US$2.6 million

SINGAPORE, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Uni-Fuels Holdings Limited (NASDAQ: UFG), (“Uni-Fuels” or the “Company”), a global provider of marine fuel solutions headquartered in Singapore, today announced its unaudited financial results for the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Nine-Month 2026 Highlights

  • Revenue increased 62% to US$307.8 million, from US$190.5 million
  • Gross profit increased 128% to US$7.5 million, from US$3.3 million
  • Gross profit margin improved 0.7 percentage points to 2.4%, from 1.7%
  • Income from operations increased 1,293% to US$2.1 million, compared with US$0.2 million
  • Operating margin improved 24.0 percentage points to 28.7%, from 4.7%
  • Net income improved to US$1.5 million, compared with a net loss of US$0.03 million
  • EBITDA increased 622% to US$2.6 million, from US$0.4 million

2026 Outlook

The Company is raising its FY2026 revenue guidance to a range of US$410 million to US$430 million, from its previous guidance range of US$340 million to US$360 million, reflecting continued business growth during the first nine months of the year and management's positive outlook for the fourth quarter, with continued momentum expected to support revenue growth through the remainder of FY2026.

Management Commentary

“We are encouraged by the continued growth of our business during the first nine months of 2026,” said Koh Kuan Hua, Chief Executive Officer of Uni-Fuels. “During the third quarter of 2026, the marine fuel market continued to experience elevated oil prices and volatility. Against this backdrop, we remained focused on serving our customers, adapting to changing market conditions and exercising discipline in our commercial activities. Looking ahead to the final quarter of the year, we remain positive about our business prospects and intend to build on the momentum achieved to date, while maintaining our focus on profitability, prudent risk management and sustainable growth.”

About Uni-Fuels Holdings Limited

Uni-Fuels is a fast-growing global provider of marine fuel solutions with a growing presence across major shipping hubs, including Singapore, Seoul, Dubai, Shanghai, Limassol, and Bangkok. Established in 2021, Uni-Fuels has evolved into a dynamic, forward-thinking company delivering customer-centric, compliant, and reliable fuel solutions across global markets and time zones, supported by 24/7 operational support year-round. Backed by a globally integrated operating platform, experienced industry professionals, and an extensive global supply network, Uni-Fuels has built trusted partnerships with customers, supporting them in achieving their operational objectives and decarbonization goals amid the maritime industry’s ongoing energy transformation.

For more information, visit www.uni-fuels.com.

Definitions

Operating Margin is calculated as income from operations as a percentage of gross profit. Management believes this measure provides a meaningful assessment of operating efficiency because the Company's business model involves the trading and supply of marine fuel products, where revenue primarily reflects the pass-through cost of fuel products and may fluctuate significantly with changes in underlying commodity prices. Accordingly, management believes gross profit provides a more meaningful basis than revenue for evaluating the Company's operating performance.

Non-GAAP Financial Measures

To supplement the Company's consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles ("U.S. GAAP"), the Company presents certain non-GAAP financial measures, including earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (“EBITDA”), which management uses to evaluate the Company's financial and operating performance.

EBITDA is defined as net income (loss) before net interest expense, income tax expense, depreciation and amortization. Management believes EBITDA provides useful supplemental information to investors by removing the effects of financing activities, income taxes and certain non-cash expenses, thereby facilitating period-to-period comparisons of the Company's financial and operating performance.

The Company presents EBITDA, a non-GAAP financial measure, solely as a supplemental measure and it should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for, or superior to, the most directly comparable financial measure prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP. In addition, EBITDA may not be comparable to similarly titled measures presented by other companies because it may be calculated differently. CHICAGO, IL / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / Cosmos Health Inc. ("Cosmos Health" or the "Company") (NASDAQ:COSM), a diversified, vertically integrated global healthcare group, today announced a Facility Master Plan to expand and modernize the manufacturing facility and warehouse of its wholly owned subsidiary, Cana Laboratories S.A. ("Cana"), in Athens, Greece. The first phase, comprising a new quality control laboratory and a new GMP warehouse, commences this quarter and is targeted for completion by the third quarter of 2027.

Strategic Rationale

Cana's contract manufacturing business continues to grow. Its contract manufacturing pipeline now exceeds 32.7 million units, Cana inaugurated a new capsule-filling production line in June 2026, and the Company recently announced the addition of an automated tablet coating system. The Master Plan is designed to ensure that Cana's infrastructure keeps pace with this growth and continues to meet applicable regulatory standards.

The program is structured across ten workstreams, each with defined deliverables, spanning engineering, permitting, construction, qualification and regulatory approval.

Phase One Scope and Timeline

  • Design and permitting (Q4 2026 - Q1 2027): engineering studies, architectural and structural design, and submission of the building permit application.
  • Quality control laboratory (Q1 - Q2 2027): construction of a new laboratory for quality control testing, followed by the transfer and qualification of laboratory instruments.
  • GMP warehouse (Q2 - Q3 2027): construction of a new warehouse in place of the existing warehouse, designed to improve the flow of materials into production, followed by qualification.
  • Regulatory inspection (Q3 2027): inspection by the EOF, targeted to complete the first phase.

Subsequent Phase

Following the first phase, the Master Plan provides for a dedicated powder production area within the facility. If completed and approved by the EOF, it would expand Cana's manufacturing portfolio with a purpose-built powder production capability, broadening the range of products available to contract manufacturing partners and to the Company's proprietary brands.

CEO Commentary

Greg Siokas, CEO of Cosmos Health, stated: "Our Facility Master Plan is designed to ensure that Cana's infrastructure keeps pace with the growth of its business. A new quality control laboratory and a new GMP warehouse form the foundation of the next stage of that growth, and we have a clear, structured plan in place, targeting completion by the third quarter of 2027.

"Together with our new capsule-filling line and tablet coating system, we believe these investments position Cana to serve more partners at higher volumes, while the planned powder production area would further expand its manufacturing capabilities."

About Cosmos Health Inc.

Cosmos Health Inc. (NASDAQ: COSM), incorporated in 2009 in Nevada, is a diversified, vertically integrated global healthcare group. The Company owns a portfolio of proprietary pharmaceutical and nutraceutical brands, including Sky Premium Life®, Mediterranation®, bio-bebe®, C-Sept® and C-Scrub®. Through its subsidiary Cana Laboratories S.A., licensed under European Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and certified by the European Medicines Agency (EMA), it manufactures pharmaceuticals, food supplements, cosmetics, biocides, and medical devices within the European Union. Cosmos Health also distributes a broad line of pharmaceuticals and parapharmaceuticals, including branded generics and OTC medications, to retail pharmacies and wholesale distributors through its subsidiaries in Greece and the UK. Furthermore, the Company has established R&D partnerships targeting major health disorders such as obesity, diabetes, and cancer, enhanced by artificial intelligence drug repurposing technologies, and focuses on the R&D of novel patented nutraceuticals, specialized root extracts, proprietary complex generics, and innovative OTC products. Cosmos Health has also entered the telehealth space through the acquisition of ZipDoctor, Inc., based in Texas, USA. With a global distribution platform, the Company is currently expanding throughout Europe, Asia, and North America, and has offices and distribution centers in Thessaloniki and Athens, Greece, and in Harlow, UK. More information is available at www.cosmoshealthinc.com, www.skypremiumlife.com, www.cana.gr, www.zipdoctor.co, www.cloudscreen.gr, as well as LinkedIn and X.

NEW YORK CITY, NY / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / The Age of Parity is no longer an abstract economic theory. It is becoming visible in real time.

A recent report in The New York Times examining the impact of surging fuel costs offers another reminder of how quickly an energy shock can become an economic shock. Recent fuel-price increases in Syria triggered widespread protests after diesel prices jumped 40 percent, while gasoline and other energy costs also increased sharply.

The circumstances in Syria are particular to that country. The larger economic lesson is not.

When oil becomes more expensive or difficult to obtain, the effects do not stop at the gas pump. They move through transportation, manufacturing, agriculture, packaging, logistics and eventually the price of everyday goods.

Plastic sits directly inside that equation.

Most conventional virgin plastic begins with fossil-fuel feedstocks. Its economics are therefore connected to a global system of oil and gas production, refining, transportation and trade. When that system becomes more expensive or unpredictable, manufacturers can feel the consequences far beyond the energy market.

That is why recycling plastic increasingly needs to be viewed as an economic strategy rather than simply an environmental objective.

SMX calls this shift the Age of Parity: the point at which the economics of recycled plastic begin competing more directly with the economics of virgin plastic.

For years, the conventional argument for recycling focused primarily on waste. Use less. Throw away less. Keep plastic out of landfills and oceans.

Those objectives remain important, but they no longer tell the whole story.

The economic argument may ultimately prove just as powerful.

Every tonne of usable plastic recovered from an existing waste stream represents material that potentially does not have to begin again with newly extracted fossil resources. Recycling creates the possibility of treating material already circulating through an economy as feedstock for the next generation of products.

That can turn waste into domestic inventory.

And in an era of volatile energy prices and disrupted supply chains, inventory matters.

THE NEW ECONOMICS OF PLASTIC

The Age of Parity changes the calculation because virgin plastic does not exist independently of the forces reshaping global energy markets.

Oil volatility and supply disruptions can affect the cost and availability of virgin material. Recycled plastic creates another potential supply source: material already contained in products, packaging and waste streams.

But for recycled plastic to function as a dependable industrial commodity, markets need more than supply. They need proof.

Manufacturers need to know what they are purchasing. Brands need evidence behind recycled-content claims. Regulators need information that can be audited. Buyers need a way to distinguish verified material from unsupported claims.

SMX's molecular marking and digital traceability technology is designed to give physical materials an identity that can remain connected to them through a supply chain. Molecular markers can be linked to digital records containing information about origin, composition and movement.

SMX's Digital Material Passport extends that identity into a digital record designed to travel with the material through its lifecycle. Instead of relying solely on paperwork or claims made at individual points in a supply chain, the passport is intended to connect physical plastic with information about what it is, where it came from and how it has moved through the system.

The company's Plastic Cycle Token (PCT)adds another component. It is designed to represent verified plastic-cycle activity digitally, connecting authenticated physical material with a tokenized record. Together, molecular identification, the Digital Material Passport and PCT are intended to create a bridge between physical recycling and the data needed to document it.

FROM WASTE STREAM TO SUPPLY STREAM

The Age of Parity reframes recycling from the final stop in a product's life to the beginning of another supply cycle.

Packaging, bottles, textiles and consumer products contain material that has already been manufactured. Recovering it does not eliminate the need for virgin plastic or insulate manufacturers from energy costs. It does create another potential source of raw material.

A manufacturer able to incorporate verified recycled material gains another procurement option. A country capable of recovering and reusing its plastic waste gains access to a material resource already within its borders.

The objective is not to declare recycled plastic universally cheaper than virgin plastic. Prices vary by polymer, geography, energy costs, processing requirements and market conditions. The larger change is that recycled plastic can increasingly be evaluated as an industrial input rather than simply an environmental substitute.

THE MATERIAL IS ALREADY HERE

Plastic presents an unusual opportunity because so much potential raw material is already in circulation. The question is whether economies can capture, identify and reuse it.

Technology alone cannot accomplish that. Collection systems, recycling infrastructure, manufacturers, regulators and markets all have roles to play. SMX's role is focused on identity and verification: connecting physical material with a record intended to remain useful as that material moves through successive cycles.

That matters because circularity ultimately depends on knowing what came back.

Plastic that can be recovered, identified, verified and reused is not merely waste diverted from a landfill. It is a resource that does not have to be created from scratch.

That is what the Age of Parity ultimately represents: not the end of virgin plastic or oil, but the emergence of a competing model in which yesterday's products can become tomorrow's raw materials.

In a world being reminded how quickly resource prices can change, throwing that material away is becoming increasingly difficult to justify.

ABOUT SMX (SECURITY MATTERS) PLC

SMX (Security Matters) PLC (NASDAQ:SMX) develops molecular traceability and material authentication technologies designed to strengthen supply-chain transparency and integrity across global industries. Its platform embeds invisible molecular markers directly into physical materials-including solids, liquids, and gases-allowing them to carry a persistent identity that can be detected and verified throughout their lifecycle.

QP

Stephen House (P.Geo.), Vice President of Exploration for Benton Resources Inc., the 'Qualified Person' under National Instrument 43-101, has approved the scientific and technical disclosure in this news release and prepared or supervised its preparation.

QA/QC Protocols

Core and rock samples, including standards, blanks and duplicates, are submitted to Eastern Analytical Ltd., Springdale, Newfoundland for preparation and analysis. All samples were acquired by saw-cut (channels/drill core) with one-half submitted for assay and one-half retained for reference, or hand (rocks) and delivered, by Benton personnel, in sealed bags, to the Springdale lab, which is an accredited assay lab that conforms to the requirements of ISO/IEC 17025. Samples are analyzed by Au Fire assay @ 30 g + ICP-34 method that delivers a 34-element package utilizing a 200 mg subsample totally dissolved in four acids and analyzed by ICP-OES analytical technique. Overlimits are analyzed using the atomic absorption method, using a 0.200 g to 2.00 g of sample, digested with three acids. All reported assays are uncut. Eastern achieved ISO 17025 accreditation in February 2014 (for more details on the scope of accreditation visit the CALA website). Grab samples are selective in nature and may not represent the average mineralization of a bedrock exposure.

Benton Resources is a well-financed mineral exploration company listed on the TSX Venture Exchange under the symbol BEX. Benton is currently planning a spinout to shareholders of its high-grade Great Burnt copper-gold project, has a diversified, highly prospective property portfolio and holds large equity positions in other mining companies that are advancing high-quality assets. Whenever possible, BEX retains net smelter return (NSR) royalties with potential long-term cash flow.

Benton is focused on advancing its Dominion Copper-Zinc-Gold project, Victoria West/South Gold Projects, Stoney Caldera Copper-Gold Project and its various Hydrogen-Helium projects on the west coast of Newfoundland.

New Leadership Safeguards Significant Tax Assets to Shield Future Taxable Income and Support Plan to Return PetMeds to Sustainable Profitability and Drive Shareholder Value

Concurrently Terminates Prior Limited Duration Shareholder Rights Plan

DELRAY BEACH, Fla., Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- PetMed Express, Inc., dba PetMeds and parent company of PetCareRx, (Nasdaq: PETS) (the “Company”), today announced that its Board of Directors has approved the adoption of a Tax Benefit Preservation Plan (or “the plan”) which is effective immediately. The plan is specifically tailored to protect and preserve PetMeds’ potentially valuable tax assets primarily associated with net operating loss carryforwards or NOLs that could be utilized in certain circumstances to offset PetMeds’ future taxable income and reduce its future federal income tax liability.

Concurrently, the Board approved the immediate termination of PetMeds’ prior limited duration shareholder rights plan, originally adopted on December 3, 2024, by accelerating its final expiration date from the close of business on December 2, 2026 to 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time on November 27, 2026. Accordingly, all Rights issued thereunder have expired, without any consideration or payment being made in respect thereof, and no person has any further rights, obligations, or liabilities thereunder, except for those provisions of that rights plan that by their express terms survive termination (including, without limitation, the indemnification, exculpation, and limitation of liability obligations of PetMeds to the Rights Agent).

New Leadership Mandate and Strategic Rationale for Protecting and Preserving NOLs

Following the appointment of Jeff Willard as PetMeds’ President and Chief Executive Officer, the new leadership of PetMeds reviewed its operations, capital structure, and asset base to optimize the use of all assets and establish a direct, clear path back to sustainable profitability and growth. As part of this asset-optimization strategy, management identified PetMeds’ accumulated NOLs as a balance sheet asset that needed to be protected and preserved.

Over the approximately two years since the adoption of the prior rights plan, PetMeds has incurred operating losses that generated significant federal NOL carryforwards. Relative to PetMeds’ current market capitalization, these tax attributes represent a material and potentially valuable corporate asset. Because an “ownership change” under Section 382 of the Internal Revenue Code (“Section 382”) could severely restrict or permanently eliminate PetMeds’ ability to utilize these tax attributes, the Board determined that adopting a Tax Benefit Preservation Plan directly supports leadership’s plans to optimize the use of all assets, return PetMeds to sustainable profitability and growth, and drive long-term shareholder value.

“Since taking the helm in September, my top priority has been conducting a comprehensive review of our strategy, execution, and balance sheet to identify every available lever to restore PetMeds to profitability, strengthen our financial position, and drive long-term shareholder value,” said Jeff Willard, President and Chief Executive Officer of PetMeds. “In a turnaround, speed matters. We are moving at a new pace, focused on repositioning the brand, upgrading our e-commerce experience, and taking costs out of the business. Our substantial net operating loss carryforwards represent a material asset that we hope to eventually monetize. As we work to return PetMeds to profitable growth, these tax assets can help shield future taxable income and drive long-term shareholder value. Adopting a Tax Benefit Preservation Plan helps protect these tax assets for the benefit of all PetMeds shareholders as our turnaround takes hold.”

Preservation of Net Operating Loss Carryforwards

As of November 2026, PetMeds had an estimate of approximately $43.4 million in federal NOL carryforwards available to offset future corporate income tax obligations. PetMeds’ ability to fully utilize these tax assets could be substantially limited if PetMeds undergoes an “ownership change” as defined under Section 382.

In general, an ownership change occurs under Section 382 if the aggregate percentage stock ownership of one or more “5-percent shareholders” (as defined for tax purposes) increases by more than 50 percentage points over a rolling three-year period over the lowest percentage of stock owned by such shareholders during that period.

In order to protect PetMeds’ NOLs from being limited or permanently lost under Section 382, the Tax Benefit Preservation Plan is intended to reduce the likelihood of an unintended “ownership change” occurring by deterring any person or group from acquiring beneficial ownership of 4.9% or more of PetMeds’ outstanding common stock without the approval of the Board. PetMeds’ Tax Benefit Preservation Plan does not, however, block anyone from buying or selling PetMeds’ common stock. Accordingly, there can be no assurance that the Tax Benefit Preservation Plan will prevent an “ownership change.” PetMeds’ Tax Benefit Preservation Plan is similar to those plans adopted by numerous other public companies with significant NOLs.

Key Terms of the Tax Benefit Preservation Plan

Under the terms of the Tax Benefit Preservation Plan, PetMeds will distribute to its shareholders one Series B preferred stock purchase right for each share of PetMeds’ common stock held as of the close of business on December 7, 2026. Any shares of common stock issued after the December 7, 2026 record date will be issued together with associated preferred stock purchase rights.

Under the Tax Benefit Preservation Plan, the rights will initially trade with PetMeds’ common stock. The rights will generally become exercisable only if a person (or any persons acting as a group) acquires beneficial ownership of 4.9% or more of PetMeds’ outstanding common stock, without the approval of the Board, after the first public announcement by PetMeds of the adoption of the Tax Benefit Preservation Plan. A person or group who acquires, without the approval of the Board, beneficial ownership of 4.9% or more of PetMeds’ outstanding common stock could be subject to significant dilution.

If the preferred stock purchase rights become exercisable, all holders of rights, other than the person or group triggering the rights, will be entitled to purchase PetMeds’ common stock at a 50% discount. The Board also has the option to cause the exchange of one share of common stock for each preferred stock purchase right held (other than the rights held by the person or group triggering the rights). Preferred stock purchase rights held by the person or group triggering the rights will become null and void and will not be exercisable, exchangeable, or transferable.

Shareholders who beneficially owned 4.9% or more of PetMeds’ outstanding common stock prior to the first public announcement by PetMeds of the adoption of the Tax Benefit Preservation Plan will not trigger any penalties under the Tax Benefit Preservation Plan so long as they do not acquire beneficial ownership of any additional shares of common stock (other than pursuant to a stock split, stock dividend, reclassification, or similar transaction effected by PetMeds) at a time when they still beneficially own 4.9% or more of such common stock. The Board also has the discretion to exempt any acquisition of PetMeds’ common stock from the provisions of the Tax Benefit Preservation Plan.

The preferred stock purchase rights and the Tax Benefit Preservation Plan will expire no later than November 25, 2029 unless the plan is extended. The preferred stock purchase rights and the Tax Benefit Preservation Plan may also expire on an earlier date upon the occurrence of other events, including a determination by the PetMeds Board that the Tax Benefit Preservation Plan is no longer necessary for the preservation of PetMeds’ tax attributes, PetMeds’ tax attributes are fully utilized or no longer available under applicable tax law, or the plan is no longer in the best interests of PetMeds and its shareholders. The preferred stock purchase rights may also be redeemed, exchanged, or terminated prior to their expiration.

PetMeds intends to submit the Tax Benefit Preservation Plan for ratification by PetMeds’ shareholders at its 2027 Annual Meeting of Shareholders. The date of PetMeds’ 2027 Annual Meeting of Shareholders has not yet been announced.

Additional Information

Additional information with respect to the termination of the prior rights plan and the adoption of the Tax Benefit Preservation Plan will be contained in the related Current Reports on Form 8-K and Registration Statements on Form 8-A that PetMeds will file with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Copies of these documents can be obtained free of charge, when available, at the SEC’s website, www.sec.gov, and at PetMeds’ website, www.PetMeds.com.

About PetMed Express, Inc.

Founded in 1996, PetMeds is a pioneer in the direct-to-consumer pet healthcare sector. As a trusted national online pharmacy, PetMeds is licensed across all 50 states and staffed with expert pharmacists dedicated to supporting pet wellness, pets and pet parents, and the veterinarians who serve them. Through its PetMeds family of brands and through its PetCareRx subsidiary, the Company offers a comprehensive range of pet health solutions - including top-brand and generic pharmaceuticals, compounded medications, and better-for-your-pet OTC supplements and nutrition. Focused on value, convenience, and care, PetMeds and PetCareRx empower pet parents to help their dogs, cats, and horses live longer, healthier lives. Salt Lake City, Utah, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- TruGolf Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: TRUG), today announced a 1-for-5 reverse split of its Class A common stock. The reverse stock split was approved by the Company’s Board of Directors in accordance with Section 78.207 of the Nevada Revised Statutes and is intended to enable the Company to regain compliance with the $1.00 minimum bid price requirement for continued listing on The Nasdaq Capital Market. Beginning on December 1, 2026, the Company’s Class A common stock will continue to trade on The Nasdaq Capital Market on a split adjusted basis under the trading symbol “TRUG” but will trade under the following new CUSIP number: 243733706.

As a result of the reverse stock split, every 5 shares of Class A common stock issued and outstanding as of the effective date will be automatically combined into one share of Class A common stock. No fractional shares will be issued if, as a result of the reverse stock split, a stockholder would otherwise become entitled to a fractional share because the number of shares of Class A common stock they hold before the reverse stock split is not evenly divisible by the split ratio. Instead, each stockholder will be entitled to receive a cash payment in lieu of a fractional share.

The reverse stock split will reduce the number of shares of outstanding Class A common stock from approximately 2.9 million shares, the number of shares outstanding as of the date hereof, to approximately 0.57 million shares. The par value of the Class A common stock will remain unchanged and the number of authorized shares of Class A common stock will be proportionately reduced to 2 million shares. The reverse split affects all stockholders uniformly and will not alter any common stockholder’s percentage interest in the Company’s equity, except to the extent that the reverse split results in some common stockholders owning a fractional share as described above.

NEW YORK CITY, NY / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / America's industrial strength has long been fueled by a willingness to challenge conventional thinking, embrace emerging technologies and transform scientific breakthroughs into practical commercial solutions. From advances in manufacturing to the digital revolution, that entrepreneurial mindset has helped shape the nation's economic identity.

Now, SMX (Security Matters) PLC (NASDAQ:SMX)(NASDAQ:SMXWW) is bringing that same spirit to artificial intelligence, developing a specialized scientific platform designed to help industries address complex material challenges while opening new possibilities for technological innovation.

Known as SMX Scientific Intelligence (SMX SCI), the platform takes a distinct approach to AI. Instead of concentrating on general-purpose applications, it is being developed to address the scientific and technical requirements of industrial material development, chemical compatibility, manufacturing and material verification.

The initiative embraces a principle central to American innovation: technology delivers its greatest value when it moves beyond theory and provides solutions to real-world problems.

AI Designed for Real-World Industry

Much of the excitement surrounding artificial intelligence has centered on its ability to generate content, analyze information and automate everyday tasks. SMX SCI is being developed with a more focused mission: helping scientific and industrial teams identify, assess and optimize materials used in manufacturing.

The platform is intended to create a comprehensive scientific codex of chemical agents, additives, molecular markers and supplementary materials.

By integrating AI-driven analysis with SMX's existing scientific expertise, it aims to assess chemical properties, production requirements, manufacturing conditions and potential industrial uses.

The goal is to streamline early-stage material research, ease laboratory workloads and allow technical teams to direct testing resources toward the most promising candidates.

For manufacturers, these capabilities could translate into quicker evaluations of material suitability, more efficient product development and faster responses to technical challenges.

SMX SCI is also being designed to provide preliminary regulatory and material compatibility assessments, including requirements applicable in the United States and other major international markets.

Final determinations involving material suitability and regulatory compliance will still require appropriate testing, validation and review.

Continuing America's Tradition of Turning Ideas Into Industry

American entrepreneurship has consistently demonstrated the value of transforming scientific discoveries into commercial opportunities.

SMX's proposed platform builds on that tradition by integrating artificial intelligence with established industrial technologies rather than positioning AI as a standalone product.

The company's molecular marking technology is designed to provide physical materials with persistent identification, while its Digital Material Passport infrastructure links those materials to records of their composition, quality, origin and lifecycle history.

SMX SCI would introduce an additional layer of scientific intelligence, helping determine suitable marking agents, additives and material solutions for specific industrial applications.

Working together, these technologies are intended to connect scientific research with manufacturing, distribution, recovery and recycling operations.

The broader infrastructure has potential uses across plastics, packaging, precious metals, electronics, semiconductors and other sectors essential to modern industrial supply chains.

This combination of scientific expertise, advanced technology and practical industrial applications reflects the resourcefulness that has historically distinguished American innovation.

Transforming Innovation Into Commercial Opportunity

The entrepreneurial potential of SMX SCI reaches beyond its scientific applications.

SMX anticipates introducing the platform into its internal operations during the first quarter of 2027, with full operations expected in the second quarter, contingent on successful development and testing.

The company also intends to launch a limited commercial edition during the second quarter of 2027, offering selected capabilities to customers around the world.

The proposed service would assist with material identification, additive selection, product enhancement and preliminary regulatory and compatibility evaluations.

Developed by SMX's internal team alongside specialized subcontractors, the platform brings together expertise in artificial intelligence, large language models, conversational AI and scientific data analysis.

The planned offering could create an additional commercial opportunity for SMX, expanding its activities beyond material identification and digital verification into AI-powered scientific services.

Creating the Infrastructure for Tomorrow's Materials

SMX SCI is also expected to advance the company's broader initiative to establish trusted global standards for certified and graded recycled plastics.

Through the integration of scientific intelligence, molecular marking and Digital Material Passports, SMX seeks to improve material identification, verification and lifecycle traceability.

The platform could also support AI-enabled functions connected to SMX's planned Plastic Circularity Credits, including credit eligibility evaluations, price discovery and connections between buyers and suppliers of certified recycled materials.

These standards and commercial mechanisms are still being developed.

For American industry, the larger opportunity lies in applying purpose-built artificial intelligence to some of manufacturing's most persistent challenges, from material efficiency and product development to supply chain transparency.

SMX SCI remains under development, and its eventual capabilities and commercial success will depend on testing, validation and market adoption.

Yet the vision behind the platform embodies a distinctly American philosophy: innovation is not measured simply by the technologies we invent, but by how effectively we put those inventions to work.

SMX (Security Matters) PLC (NASDAQ:SMX) develops molecular traceability and material authentication technologies designed to strengthen supply-chain transparency and integrity across global industries. Its platform embeds invisible molecular markers directly into physical materials, including solids, liquids and gases, allowing them to carry a persistent identity that can be detected and verified throughout their lifecycle.

The exhibition underscores the Company's continued advancement of its AI-driven smart pet care strategy and its global distribution. Through its distribution network across 35 countries and regions, Dogness aims to commercialize its AI-powered pet products and capture new growth opportunities in the smart pet care industry.

Extensive Global Distribution Network Supports AI Product Commercialization

Dogness's channel network now covers 35 countries and regions worldwide. It sells through global retailers and specialized pet channels including Walmart, Costco, Petco and Pet Valu, online platforms such as Amazon and Chewy, as well as brand and industry partners like Velcro. This broad network and the Company's long-standing relationships provide a foundation for presenting products, gathering market feedback and exploring new collaborations. They also support Dogness's efforts to introduce its new AI products to different markets and adapt its product portfolio to local needs, strengthening its relationships with major international retailers.

Driving AI Innovation in Smart Pet Care Through a Structured Matrix of AI Products

While strengthening its established pet supplies business, Dogness continues to expand the development and production of AI-enabled pet products. The Company continues to invest in R&D for intelligent functions and products designed for specific pet care needs, pursuing a two-track approach that combines an established product foundation with continued AI innovation.

  • New AI Products: Advancing the AI Strategy through Smart Feeding

At CIPS 2026, Dogness showcased the F01B and F10B AI feeders, allowing attendees to explore smart feeding and scenario-based interaction features through hands-on demonstrations. The 3.6-liter F10B, built with Google Gemini, features a high-definition night-vision camera and AI-powered behavior recognition that alerts owners to unusual activity through the Dogness mobile app. The F01B offers a larger 8-liter capacity in a distinct design. AI feeders are an important entry point within the Company's expanding portfolio of AI pet products. Dogness continues to invest in R&D and refine products around real-world pet care needs, advancing the application of AI capabilities in everyday feeding scenarios.

More importantly, Dogness's AI strategy is not a collection of standalone devices but a scenario-driven product matrix. Its technical strengths are reflected in three areas: first, scenario-based interaction capabilities developed around high-frequency pet care scenarios including feeding, interaction and location tracking; second, integrated hardware-software-scenario design that enables AI features to deliver a seamless user experience throughout real-world usage journeys; and third, sustained R&D and iteration capabilities, underpinned by the Company's continued investment in intelligent function development and scenario-based product pipeline reserves. AI feeders serve as the primary entry point, as the product matrix extends into location-tracking use cases, with AI-enabled water fountains in the pipeline to form a multi-scenario AI product matrix covering feeding, hydration and location tracking.

  • Established Product Portfolio as a Robust Foundation for AI-Driven Growth

At CIPS 2026, Dogness also presented quick-release pet leashes, the slow-recovery R06 retractable leash, paw cleaner cups, training mats and reflective collars, covering everyday walking, cleaning, training and visibility needs.

The established portfolio delivers four key pillars supporting Dogness's AI product development: an established customer base and repeat-purchase relationships that create a natural on-ramp for AI products; brand recognition that lowers market education costs for new AI offerings; an integrated, in-house supply chain covering design and R&D, material sourcing, manufacturing and quality control, which supports production of AI products with consistent quality and effective cost control; and existing sales channels, including distributor networks, retail outlets and e-commerce operations, to support the distribution and promotion of AI products.

Furthermore, Dogness's traditional and AI businesses unlock opportunities for cross-selling and mutual promotion. Channel credibility and user relationships built through its established product lineup help AI products gain market traction. In turn, AI products elevate the brand's technological positioning and customer value, reinforcing the established product portfolio. As such, Dogness has built a growth framework wherein its established product portfolio stabilizes the core business and its structured AI product matrix is intended to drive incremental growth.

Silong Chen, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Dogness, commented: "CIPS 2026 enables us to leverage our well-established worldwide sales network and customer base, supported by end-to-end R&D and manufacturing systems, to further advance our strategic transformation from a traditional global pet products manufacturer into a global AI-powered smart pet care technology company, and accelerate the global commercialization of AI-powered pet products."

Dogness (International) Corporation was founded in 2003 from the belief that dogs and cats are important, well-loved family members. KeyBank shares warning signs and practical steps for avoiding phishing, fake shopping sites, payment app scams and other holiday fraud

CLEVELAND, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As holiday shopping picks up, so do opportunities for scammers.

Consumers shopping online, tracking packages, buying gift cards or donating to charities can encounter increasingly convincing fraud attempts. Scammers are also using artificial intelligence to create fake retail websites, emails, text messages and even AI-generated voices designed to impersonate trusted companies or people.

Knowing what to look for can help consumers recognize potential fraud before they share personal information or send money.

What are the most common holiday shopping scams?

Here are several scams consumers should watch for during the holiday season:

Bank imposter scams. Fraudsters may call, text or email pretending to represent a consumer's bank. They may claim there has been a suspicious transaction or login attempt, then ask for a one-time passcode, login credentials or debit card information. KeyBank will not initiate a call or text asking for your online banking username or password. KeyBank also will not ask a client to send money to themselves using Zelle®, an account transfer or a wire payment, or request remote access to your computer or mobile device. However, in some cases, we will call to verify your identity by asking for a one-time passcode that is sent to your mobile device.

Phishing and smishing scams. Fraudulent emails and text messages can look like legitimate communications from retailers, banks or delivery companies. Scammers may also use AI to create convincing fake retail websites and communications intended to capture debit card, credit card or other personal information. A common example is a fake package-delivery message asking for payment to release or redeliver an order.

Vishing and AI voice scams. Criminals can use AI-generated voices in phone calls to impersonate customer service representatives, delivery companies, family members or others in an effort to obtain sensitive information.

Payment app scams. Consumers should be cautious when an unfamiliar seller asks for payment through Zelle®, Venmo, Cash App, wire transfer or cryptocurrency. Recovering money sent to a fraudulent seller through these methods can be difficult.

Online marketplace scams. Fraudsters may advertise popular holiday gifts at unusually low prices, then request advance payment through a payment app, gift card or cryptocurrency before disappearing.

Gift card scams. Criminals may tamper with gift cards displayed on retail racks or convince victims to provide gift card numbers over the phone to make supposedly urgent payments.

Charity scams. The season of giving can also attract criminals impersonating legitimate charities or disaster-relief organizations through phone calls, texts, emails and social media.

5 ways to shop more safely this holiday season

A few habits can make it harder for scammers to succeed:

  1. Be skeptical of unexpected communications. Don't automatically trust an unsolicited call, email or text, even if it appears legitimate. Avoid clicking unfamiliar links or attachments and independently verify the communication using a known phone number, website or app.
  2. Monitor financial accounts regularly. Reviewing account activity frequently can help consumers identify unauthorized transactions sooner. KeyBank recommends clients check their accounts daily and report unauthorized activity immediately.
  3. Turn on multi-factor authentication. MFA provides another layer of account security by requiring an additional form of verification when signing in.
  4. Use secure internet connections. Avoid conducting financial transactions over public Wi-Fi. A secure Wi-Fi connection or virtual private network, or VPN, can help protect data.
  5. Look for buyer protection. When shopping through online marketplaces, consider platforms offering buyer protections and avoid paying sellers who cannot be independently verified.

Holiday scam warning signs consumers shouldn't ignore

Consumers should pause when they encounter:

  • A deal that seems too good to be true
  • An unexpected call, email or text
  • Pressure to send money or act immediately
  • Requests to keep a transaction secret
  • Requests for passwords, codes or sensitive financial information
  • Demands for payment through gift cards, cryptocurrency or payment apps
  • Last-minute requests to change payment information
  • Requests for remote access to a computer or device

These behaviors can indicate an attempted scam.

What should you do if you think you've been scammed?

Speed matters.

Consumers who believe they have been targeted or have already sent money should contact their financial institution immediately and report suspected fraud to the retailer and appropriate authorities. KeyBank clients can contact the KeyBank Fraud Client Service Center at 1-800-433-0124. Dial 711 for TTY/TRS.

Additional information about emerging scams, account security and fraud prevention is available at key.com/fraud.

Ultimately, one of the strongest defenses against holiday fraud is taking a moment before responding. An unexpected message, urgent request or unusually attractive deal is worth verifying independently before clicking a link, providing information or sending money.

NEW YORK, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Blue Gold Limited (Nasdaq: BGL, BGLWW) (“Blue Gold” or the “Company”) today announced that it has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Current Technology (TripleBolt Technology Corporation) (“Current”), an AI-native software and consulting firm, to bring agentic AI payments into Blue Gold’s new gold-powered banking app. Under the collaboration, Blue Gold customers will be able to authorize AI agents to initiate and manage payments, bill pay, transfers and purchases on their behalf, within spending limits and permissions they set and can revoke at any time. Payments are expected to settle in gold or gold-backed balances where available, combining the stability of gold with the speed and convenience of AI-driven commerce.

According to Deloitte, by 2030, agentic commerce could drive up to $17.5 trillion in commerce, making it a pivotal force in the future of payments and consumer engagement.

The payments layer that powers this shift is growing quickly. According to DataM Intelligence, the global agentic payments market was valued at USD 18 million in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 398.99 billion by 2035, a compound annual growth rate of 172%. North America led the market with an estimated 36.8% share in 2025. Growth is driven by AI agents making autonomous purchases, new agentic commerce protocols and payment standards, and rising demand for frictionless, personalized checkout.

“The question isn’t whether agentic payments will transform financial services—it’s whether your organization will lead this transformation or be disrupted by it,” said Kevin Clark, Executive Chairman of Blue Gold. “The infrastructure is being built, the market is expanding rapidly, and early movers are already gaining competitive advantages.”

“Agentic payments are moving from concept to real money movement, and the institutions that build them in now will set the standard,” said Erin Barton, Co-Founder and Chief Operating Officer of Current. “Blue Gold has the gold infrastructure and a clear vision for modern banking. Our job is to deliver agents that customers can trust with their money: clear permissions, strong controls and a full audit trail behind every transaction. We are proud to help Blue Gold bring that to market.”

The collaboration is expected to cover agentic payment experience design, AI agent development, integration with Blue Gold’s banking and gold settlement infrastructure, support for emerging agentic commerce standards, and controls for consent, fraud prevention and compliance. Company to contribute Greenlandic project-development experience to selected Nordic forum and undertake separate stakeholder engagement in Nuuk

CHARLOTTE, NC, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Greenland Mines Ltd (Nasdaq: GRML; FSE: HK6) (“Greenland Mines” or the “Company”) today announced that President Bo Møller Stensgaard has accepted an invitation to join the “Building Nordic Value Chains” panel discussion at the Nordic Forum on Raw Materials (“RAW”) conference, “Strengthening Collaboration on Critical and Strategic Raw Materials,” in Nuuk, Greenland, December 8–10, 2026. Dr. Stensgaard and Robert Møller, the Company’s Nuuk-based Permitting & Community Officer, plan to attend the conference.

Convened through personal invitations, the conference will bring together a selected group of senior representatives and experts from industry, academia, research organisations, public authorities and governments across the Nordic region. Organizers have identified participants based on their experience, expertise, and ability to contribute to a strategic dialogue on the future of Nordic critical and strategic raw-material cooperation.

Greenland Mines views the invitation to contribute to the panel as recognition of the practical perspective it brings through its active development projects, Greenlandic presence, and relationships across the Nordic minerals sector.

Connecting Greenlandic Resources with Nordic Industrial Strength

The conference will examine how closer Nordic cooperation can support research, innovation, investment, skills, and competitive mineral-based value chains. RAW is coordinated by Nordic mining and minerals industry associations and supported by Nordic Innovation, an organization within the Nordic Council of Ministers. Its network connects industry, research, finance, and public-sector stakeholders across the Nordic countries and autonomous regions.

Through the panel discussion, Greenland Mines intends to contribute experience from advancing the Sarfartoq neodymium-praseodymium rare earth project in southwest Greenland and the Skaergaard palladium-platinum-gold project in southeast Greenland. Its focus will be on connecting Greenlandic resources with Nordic expertise and industrial capacity, and on the practical requirements for moving projects forward: technical studies, permitting, environmental understanding, infrastructure, financing, and meaningful local participation.

“The Nordic region has the resources, technical expertise and industrial capabilities to make a much greater contribution to critical-mineral supply security. The challenge is to connect those strengths and translate them into responsible projects and competitive supply chains,” said Bo Møller Stensgaard, President of Greenland Mines.

“The invitation to join the ‘Building Nordic Value Chains’ panel gives us an opportunity to bring a Greenland-focused developer’s perspective to this strategic discussion,” Stensgaard continued. “Our focus is what it takes to move from geological potential and resource development to technically sound, financeable and permitted mining projects - and where Nordic cooperation can make a practical difference.”

Grounded in Greenland, Connected Across the North Atlantic

The Company’s delegation combines project-development leadership with a local perspective. Robert Møller, who is Greenlandic/Inuit and based in Nuuk, brings local knowledge and a focus on permitting and community engagement to the Company’s participation.

Alongside the conference, Greenland Mines is arranging separate meetings in Nuuk with local institutional stakeholders, authorities, and international representatives in Nuuk to discuss the Company’s activities, responsible project development and opportunities for local value creation, and to provide updates on its ongoing international partnership activities.

“Our presence in Nuuk is about more than participating in a conference,” Stensgaard continued. “It is an opportunity to listen, strengthen relationships and discuss how our projects can progress responsibly and create lasting value in Greenland. With Robert based in Nuuk, we bring an ongoing local presence to that dialogue. International expertise and investment must connect with Greenlandic priorities, local communities, businesses and opportunities for people in Greenland.”

The conference’s emphasis on cross-border cooperation aligns with Greenland Mines’ North Atlantic Critical Metals Corridor vision: connecting responsibly developed Greenlandic resources with Nordic and wider allied capabilities in research, technology, logistics, processing, investment and industrial markets.

Sarfartoq and Skaergaard provide complementary foundations for that vision, spanning rare earth magnet materials and palladium, platinum and gold. The Company sees Nordic collaboration as an opportunity to strengthen the technical and commercial relationships needed to advance these projects while supporting potential economic activity in Greenland and the wider North Atlantic.

“Supply security will not be built through isolated projects or policy announcements alone,” Dr. Stensgaard added. “It requires resources, infrastructure, technology, capital and local participation to move together. That is the practical cooperation we want to help build - and why this dialogue in Nuuk matters.”

Participation in the conference, panel discussion and separate stakeholder meetings does not constitute endorsement of Greenland Mines by the organisers, meeting counterparties or participating institutions and does not imply any financing, permitting, commercial agreement or partnership commitment.

Greenland Mines Ltd is listed on Nasdaq and develops mineral assets in Greenland, including the Skaergaard precious-metals project in southeast Greenland and the Sarfartoq neodymium-praseodymium rare earths project in southwest Greenland. Its North Atlantic Critical Metals Corridor strategy seeks to connect Greenland resources with processing capacity and industrial customers in the United States and allied countries.   • Intranasal foralumab has been well tolerated across all studies, with no serious adverse events related to study drug

BOSTON, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Tiziana Life Sciences, Ltd. (Nasdaq: TLSA) (“Tiziana” or the “Company”), a biotechnology company developing breakthrough immunomodulation therapies with its lead development candidate, intranasal foralumab, a fully human anti-CD3 monoclonal antibody, today announced the submission of its annual Development Safety Update Report (DSUR) to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). This DSUR (dated September 2, 2024 to September 30, 2026) reports no drug-related serious adverse events after a cumulative exposure of 48.1 patient-years, highlighting the safety and tolerability data profile of intranasal foralumab in treating neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative diseases, including non-active secondary progressive multiple sclerosis (na-SPMS), Alzheimer’s disease (AD), multiple system atrophy (MSA), and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).

“We have seen 48.1 patient-years of cumulative foralumab exposure with no study drug-related serious adverse events, a milestone that reinforces the safety of our intranasal approach,” said Ivor Elrifi, Chief Executive Officer of Tiziana. “Acceptable safety and tolerability continue to be observed across our CNS programs, supporting continued clinical development. We believe that this favorable safety and tolerability profile additionally paves the way for exploring the use of nasal foralumab, not only as a mono-therapy, but also as a multiple sclerosis combination therapy for patients on anti-CD20 approved therapies such as Ocrevus® (ocrelizumab). We have previously announced a memorandum of understanding (MOU) signed with King Abdullah International Medical Research Center (KAIMRC) in Saudi Arabia, with our intention to collaborate on a clinical trial evaluating this combination therapy.”

Key highlights from the submission include:

  • Expanded Access Program (IND 161148): As of 30 September 2026, fourteen (14) patients with na-SPMS were treated with nasal foralumab at Brigham and Women’s Hospital. They received nasal foralumab at 50 or 100 micrograms per dosing day (6 days per three-week cycle) for durations ranging from 23 weeks to 4.7 years. The total cumulative patient exposure in this study is 32.1 patient-years.

  • TILS-021 Randomized Trial and TILS-022 Open-Label Extension: This randomized, double-blind trial in patients with na-SPMS administers foralumab intranasally at doses of either 50 or 100 µg in addition to placebo. The trial completed enrollment (48 patients total) in the summer of 2026, with the last patient dosed on 17 August 2026. Thirty (30) patients were administered foralumab. The total estimated cumulative patient exposure in this study and the open-label extension is 10.25 patient-years.

  • Alzheimer’s Disease (TILS-024 and Expanded Access): Tiziana initiated study TILS-024 in Q4 2025. This randomized, controlled, double-blind study uses a 3:1 treatment ratio (50 µg intranasal foralumab versus placebo) with the same dosing schedule. It is estimated that eleven (11) patients have received nasal foralumab in the reporting period, with an estimated cumulative patient exposure of 1.4 years. One (1) patient with moderate AD continued treatment in a single-patient expanded access IND (IND 172400) at 50 micrograms intranasally per dosing day (6 days per three-week cycle) and has completed 93 weeks of therapy (1.8 total patient-years).

  • Multiple System Atrophy (TILS-025): Initiated in the second half of 2025, this open-label study uses the same dosing schedule. Seven (7) patients have received nasal foralumab for 3–8 weeks duration, with a cumulative patient exposure of 2.50 years.

  • ALS (TILS-ALS-01): Initiated in Q3 2026, this randomized, controlled, double-blind study uses a 3:1 treatment ratio (50 µg intranasal foralumab versus placebo) with the same dosing schedule. It is estimated that two (2) patients have received nasal foralumab in the reporting period, with an estimated cumulative patient exposure of 0.04 years.

In these studies investigating intranasal foralumab in central nervous system (CNS) diseases, favorable safety and tolerability have been observed. During the reporting period, no new risks were identified that resulted in significant protocol amendments for any of the clinical studies. The types and frequency of reported adverse events are generally consistent with those from previous reporting periods.

In conclusion, no substantive changes to the previous knowledge of foralumab safety and tolerability when administered intranasally to patients with CNS disease were identified during the reporting period. The benefit:risk for intranasal foralumab remains favorable in these patients and continued clinical development in CNS patients is warranted. No new actions to address the safety of intranasally delivered foralumab have arisen from the current reporting period.

The cumulative estimated drug exposure for these subjects is 48.1 patient-years. No serious adverse events so far attributed to study drug in nasal foralumab CNS studies. The safety profile of intranasal foralumab aligns with prior studies of foralumab administered intravenously (IV) in healthy volunteers, patients with Crohn’s disease, and kidney transplant recipients. Unlike IV administration, which has been linked to infusion-related reactions seen with other anti-CD3 monoclonal antibodies, nasal delivery of foralumab appears to have better tolerability, with no such issues observed to date.

About Foralumab
Foralumab, a fully human anti-CD3 monoclonal antibody, is a biological drug candidate that has been shown to stimulate T regulatory cells when dosed intranasally. The recently announced INFORM-MS Phase 2a, placebo controlled, double blind trial met its dual primary endpoints for (1) statistically significant reduction (p=0.0168) in microglial activation as measured by TSPO PET imaging in patients treated with 50 ug nasal foralumab as compared to placebo and (2) safety/tolerability. Foralumab treated subjects showed statistically and clinically significant improvements in Modified Fatigue Impact Scale (MFIS) scores compared with their own baseline scores after only 12 weeks of drug therapy. Subjects treated with 50 ug nasal foralumab saw a -6.17 point decrease from baseline (p=0.035), and those treated with 100 ug experienced a -7.18 decrease from baseline (p=0.040). At present, 14 patients with Non-Active Secondary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis (na-SPMS) have been dosed in an open-label intermediate sized Expanded Access (EA) Program (NCT06802328) with either an improvement or stability of disease seen within 6 months in all patients. Intranasal foralumab is also currently being studied in additional Phase 2 trials in Alzheimer’s disease (AD), multiple system atrophy (MSA), and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Intranasal foralumab is the only fully human anti-CD3 monoclonal antibody (mAb) currently in clinical development. Immunomodulation by intranasal foralumab represents a novel avenue for the treatment of neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative human diseases.[1],[2]
